item.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year
item.description: When ICE agents show up at a school, educators rely on a patchwork of policies to know what to do. This year, many state legislatures tried to update those policies.

item.title: Kennedy Center plans Ticketmaster switch, raising conflict of interest concerns
item.description: The Kennedy Center's former president Richard Grenell was a paid board member of Ticketmaster's parent company at the same time the two parties were negotiating.

item.title: Morning news brief
item.description: Scott Colom has won the U.S. Senate race in Mississippi, The White House is getting ready to fight new Democratic oversight, U.S.-mediated talks between Russia and Ukraine have wrapped up.

item.title: Some states get a head start on upcoming federal hemp ban
item.description: A federal ban on Hemp-derived THC products is set to take effect in less than a month. But some states have moved to start their own ban earlier.

item.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
item.description: The SS United States broke trans-Atlantic speed records. On Wednesday, it was sunk off the Florida coast and will become a diving destination and home for marine life.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.
